canon.rule: The Force is an energy field created by all living things, flowing through everything and binding the galaxy together.
Sensitivity to the Force is something a person is born with — it cannot be handed to anyone — and in the films it shows as midi-chlorians, tiny living things in every cell.
Training matters more than raw talent: an untrained sensitive gets flashes and lucky instincts, never control.
The Force answers calm, breathing and letting go, and it slips away from anyone who grabs at it in a temper.
The light side is fed by patience, compassion and service to life, and it asks its users to let go of fear and of wanting to own things.
The dark side is fed by fear, anger, hatred and the wish to control, and it offers quick power at a steep price to the one who takes it.
Falling to the dark side happens in small steps rather than one moment, and coming back from it is possible but very hard.
A trained Force user can move objects with the mind — lifting, pushing, pulling, holding — limited by focus and belief rather than muscle.
The Force sharpens reflexes and lets its users leap, run and react far past ordinary limits.
A Force user can sense living things nearby and feel danger a heartbeat before it arrives.
Some Force users glimpse visions of things to come, but a vision shows one possible future, not a fixed one — and acting on it rashly is often how it comes true.
The mind trick pushes a suggestion into a weak-willed mind; strong-willed beings such as Hutts and Toydarians shrug it off, and droids have no mind to push, so it never works on them.
Force users can steady, strengthen or calm others, and the rarest of them can heal an injury at real cost to themselves.
Dark-side powers such as Force lightning exist, and every use tightens the dark side's grip on whoever uses it.
The Jedi are an order of Force users who serve life and keep the peace, trained from childhood and taught to master fear rather than feed it.
The Sith are the dark mirror of the Jedi, seeking power through passion and domination, and by their own old rule there are only ever two at a time — a master and an apprentice.
A lightsaber is a blade of pure energy thrown from a handmade hilt, and the heart of the weapon is a kyber crystal.
Kyber crystals are rare, living, Force-attuned crystals that must be found and bonded with before they will light a blade for anyone.
A kyber crystal is colourless until it is attuned, and the bond decides the blade's colour — blue and green are the commonest Jedi blades, with purple, yellow and others besides.
A dark-side user can 'bleed' a crystal by pouring anger and pain into it, turning the blade red, and a bled crystal can afterwards be healed back by someone who understands that pain.
Building your own lightsaber is a rite of passage, and a Jedi treats the finished weapon as part of themselves rather than as a tool to lend around.
A lightsaber blade has no weight to swing, only balance, and given a moment's work it cuts through nearly anything — metal, stone, a sealed blast door.
A few rare substances defy it: beskar, the Mandalorian iron, turns a blade aside; cortosis shorts one out on contact; and phrik holds against a strike, which is why some guards carry phrik staffs.
One blade will not pass through another — lightsabers lock and clash — and a trained user can bat blaster bolts away, even back at whoever fired them.
A lit blade is dangerous in an untrained hand and burns whatever it brushes, so lightsaber training is a matter of safety long before it is a matter of duelling.
Two Force users who are close — master and apprentice, siblings, partners through many battles — can form a rare Force bond and feel each other's thoughts and pain across any distance.
A few great masters learn to return after death as a glowing blue Force ghost, able to be seen and heard by those they choose and to give advice but not to lift a finger.
A lightsaber blade cauterises what it cuts, so the wounds it leaves do not bleed.

Lightsaber hilts vary: the standard single blade, the double-bladed saber with one hilt and a blade from each end, a short shoto for the off hand, a crossguard hilt that vents two small blades at the grip, and low-powered training sabers for beginners.
The Darksaber is one of a kind — an ancient flat black blade tied to who leads Mandalore, and by Mandalorian custom it passes only to whoever defeats its bearer.
Duelists study seven classic lightsaber forms, from Soresu's patient impenetrable defence to Ataru's leaping acrobatics to Djem So's overwhelming power strikes.
Blasters fire bolts of light rather than bullets, astromech droids like R2-D2 answer in beeps and whistles, protocol droids like C-3PO talk far too much, and Wookiees roar instead of speaking words.

characters.name: Yoda
characters.role: Grand Master of the Jedi Order, teacher of Force users for some nine hundred years
characters.status: era-flagged: alive and teaching through the Clone Wars and the Empire's early years; in exile on Dagobah by the time of the Rebellion
characters.physical: very small, green-skinned and long-eared, leaning on a gimer stick; ancient and quick
characters.voice: inverts his sentences, teaches by riddle and rebuke, laughs at the wrong moment, and lands the hard truth in the fewest words
characters.motivation: passing on what he knows before the light is lost
knows: that fear is the first step toward the dark side
that a student must unlearn before they can learn
does_not_know: how much of the future the Force is hiding from him

last_seen.location: wherever the reader's era places him
last_seen.state: teaching, or waiting in exile, depending on the era chosen

characters.name: Obi-Wan Kenobi
characters.role: Jedi Knight and later Master, a duellist and negotiator
characters.status: era-flagged: a young knight during the Clone Wars; a hermit on Tatooine calling himself Ben by the Rebellion's dawn
characters.physical: bearded, in layered Jedi robes; upright bearing, tired eyes in the later years
characters.voice: dry, courteous and faintly amused — defuses a crisis with an understatement and only sounds stern when he is frightened for someone
characters.motivation: duty to the Order, and to the people he has promised to protect
knows: that patience wins more fights than aggression
that attachment is what the Order warns against and what he keeps anyway
does_not_know: how the choices of those he loves will turn out

last_seen.location: wherever the reader's era places him
last_seen.state: on a mission, or in quiet exile, depending on the era chosen

characters.name: Darth Vader
characters.role: Sith Lord and enforcer of the Empire, once the Jedi Anakin Skywalker
characters.status: era-flagged: exists only in the Imperial era; before that he is Anakin Skywalker, a Jedi
characters.physical: very tall in black armour and a helmet, cloak to the floor, breathing in a slow mechanical rhythm you hear before you see him
characters.voice: deep, unhurried and quiet; states an order once and lets the silence do the threatening
characters.motivation: order imposed by force, and a buried grief he will not look at
knows: that the dark side made him powerful
that his master does not trust him
does_not_know: that the good in him is not gone

last_seen.location: wherever the reader's era places him
last_seen.state: serving the Empire — and not present at all in stories set before it

relationships.state: ancient enemies — the same power used to serve life or to rule it
relationships.history: Both orders draw on the Force; they split long ago over whether it is to be served or commanded.

relationships.state: the standard teaching bond: one master, one apprentice, learning by travelling together
relationships.history: The Order has trained this way for a thousand generations, and the bond usually outlasts the training.

relationships.state: a genuine bond — the crystal chooses as much as it is chosen, and answers to that user afterwards
relationships.history: The crystal is found, not bought, and attuning to it is the first real test of a young Force user's patience.

locations.name: Ilum
locations.description: An ice world whose frozen caves grow kyber crystals, where young Jedi are sent to find the crystal that will become their lightsaber
locations.state: sacred to the Jedi and known to few others; a place of trial rather than of fighting

locations.name: The Jedi Temple on Coruscant
locations.description: The Order's great home on the galaxy's capital world: training halls, archives, council chamber and spires above endless city
locations.state: era-flagged — the Order's beating heart while the Jedi stand, and lost to them afterwards

locations.name: Dagobah
locations.description: A humid swamp world thick with mist, vines and life, strong in the Force and easy to hide in
locations.state: remote and unmapped; a place people come to disappear or to learn
